content.text:
Yes, plugins are still supported, but the docs only cover loading them, not writing them.

- The `@plugin` directive loads a "legacy JavaScript-based plugin", from a package name or a local path, for example `@plugin "@tailwindcss/typography";`. (`src/docs/functions-and-directives.mdx`, "Compatibility" section, `@plugin`)
- The same section says `@config` and `@plugin` exist "solely for compatibility with Tailwind CSS v3.x". They can be combined with `@theme`, `@utility` and other CSS-driven features.
- I found no v4 docs page on authoring plugins. A search for `addUtilities`, `matchUtilities` and `plugin(` only matched blog posts for v1.5 through v3.2, plus the `@plugin` mention above.

The docs don't say whether the v3 plugin API is deprecated. They only say `@plugin` is kept for v3 compatibility.

I couldn't run `graphify query` because Bash was denied, so I used Grep on the docs instead.
